ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (Title 31, Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended); Money Laundering (Control and Regulation) Act 1999; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Regulations 2018; Beneficial Ownership and Registered Agent (Information Disclosure) Regulations 2019; Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport of each proposed director, shareholder, and beneficial owner (with a signed attestation form)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document-issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by an RMI Embassy or Consulate, or Hague Apostille if the origin jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address for each beneficial owner and subscriber (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Consular Legalization (or Hague Apostille where applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the financial standing and AML status of the subscriber/beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Consular Legalization (or Hague Apostille where applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent engagement letter and due diligence questionnaire, signed by the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent (e.g., a Registered Agent authorized under the Business Corporations Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal notarization accepted; no apostille or consular legalization required when executed in the Marshall Islands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury Consolidated List, and the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit domestic watchlist. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and their close associates. Screening must include adverse-media review using recognized compliance databases (e.g., World-Check or Dow Jones), and monitoring must be refreshed on a rolling annual basis or upon any trigger event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry Online Filing System (operated by International Registries, Inc. under delegated authority from the Registrar of Corporations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All legal corporate names must be provided in English using the ISO basic Latin alphabet. Foreign-script names are permitted only as transliterated words; diacritical marks and non-Latin characters are not accepted in the official corporate name field. Approved corporate suffixes are limited to 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Company', or their standard English abbreviations 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Co.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written rejection notice within ten business days. An administrative appeal may be lodged through the licensed registered agent within thirty days of the rejection, accompanied by a memorandum explaining why the name does not create public confusion or contravene any statutory prohibition and a non-refundable USD 200 appeal fee. The Registrar shall issue a final written determination within fifteen business days, and an adverse determination may be appealed to the Minister responsible for the corporate registry within a further fifteen business days. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit a new name reservation without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for administrative management and e-commerce back-office functions; the statutory registered office must be a physical street address in the Marshall Islands maintained by the licensed registered agent, and a virtual office cannot be used as the registered office address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 1% to 5% annual probability) for a non-licensed online maternity and baby supplies retailer, but the Financial Intelligence Unit and the Registrar retain unrestricted statutory inspection powers and may require short-notice inspections of registered-agent records with at least 48 hours notification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations (via licensed RMI registered agent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations / International Registries, Inc.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee under Title 31 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code; based on authorized share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office services for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in RMI corporate service providers (USD 350 to USD 750 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML due diligence and sanctions screening for the entity and up to five natural person ultimate beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent or independent compliance provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and consular statutory charges; market benchmark for expedited handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Time-based fee at USD 250 per hour for approximately two attorney hours

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, codified in Title 32 of the RMI Revised Code (Sections 10, 15, 29, 32, 34 and 44), together with the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, with Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Business Corporations Act allows shares to be issued for lawful consideration determined by the board; no escrow account or capital deposit is required for a non-resident domestic business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation ratify and adopt the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registrar of Corporations; RESOLVED, that the registered office and registered agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands be and hereby are established and appointed; RESOLVED, that the initial share subscription and allotment be approved as set forth in the share register; RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President and [Name] be appointed Secretary/Treasurer, each to act until successors are elected; RESOLVED, that the Board is authorized to open a bank account and compensate the registered agent; and RESOLVED, that all formation documents and filings are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry online portal, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name availability request to the Registrar; verify that the proposed name is distinguishable and does not contain prohibited terms; include 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or an authorized abbreviation; upon approval, pay the reservation fee to reserve the name for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Photographic identification of incorporator or authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar flags a conflict or prohibited term, file a revised name request within 14 days; if refusal persists, request administrative review with supporting distinguishable-element evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Execute and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator(s) and an accredited Marshall Islands registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles in English setting out the corporate name, registered office address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, registered agent name, authorized share capital, initial directors and any restrictions; each incorporator signs in the presence of a notary public; the registered agent consents and countersigns where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registered agent rejects execution, cure by reperfecting signatures and resubmitting; if a substantive omission is identified, amend the Articles, re-execute and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Articles to Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, filing desk or e-filing through accredited registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed and notarized Articles together with the government filing fee; the Registrar checks statutory completeness, issues a filing receipt, and processes the incorporation in order of submission; expedited processing may be requested for an additional fee.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a query or rejection, cure identified deficiencies within 21 days; if the Registrar determines the name or registered agent is defective, file corrective Articles or alternate agent consent; appeal to the Registrar's appellate body if the rejection is not cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; verify that the registered office and registered agent appear correctly; request certified copies of the Articles and certificate for the corporate record book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, submit a written correction request to the Registrar; if the registered agent's acknowledgment is missing, coordinate with the agent to file a retroactive consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws and Organizational Board Action
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial directors and/or incorporators acting as the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting or obtain unanimous written consent; adopt bylaws; appoint officers; approve share issuance and subscription; designate bank account signatories; ratify all incorporation steps; maintain minutes in the corporate record book.
required_dossiers: Minutes of organizational meeting or unanimous written consent
Consent to act as directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory meeting formalities are defective, cure by passing a unanimous written consent that ratifies prior acts and resolves the procedural deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings and Non-Resident Exemption Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the required annual verification and registered agent details with the Registrar; maintain the corporate register and share ledger; renew registered agent appointments and government license fees; confirm non-resident status by retaining evidence that no business is conducted within the Marshall Islands.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a late-filing penalty is asserted, submit the renewal and request abatement of penalty based on reasonable cause or within the applicable statutory grace period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — non-resident online retailer has no manufacturing, distribution, or industrial facility in the Marshall Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the entity conducts online sales of maternity and baby care supplies through ecommerce platforms outside the Marshall Islands, and no local industrial operating license is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no project, installation, warehouse, or physical establishment subject to EIA regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater, VOC, or solid waste emissions are generated within Marshall Islands territory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no physical premises or employees stationed in the Marshall Islands; if the company later establishes a local office or warehouse, RMI fire safety certification, structural load inspection, and workplace clearance would be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Tax and Revenue Office (TRO), Ministry of Finance, Treasury and Planning, Majuro — administers the Income Tax Act 1989, Gross Revenue Tax and Customs Act 1990. Corporate registration: Office of the Registrar of Corporations; online corporate registry services are operated by International Registries, Inc. at https://www.register-iri.com. The TRO operates no public e-filing portal for exempt non-resident corporations; filings are paper-based in Majuro.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No TIN is required for, or issued to, an exempt non-resident Business Corporation (BC). Procedure: (1) file Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations declaring non-resident status under section 116 of the Business Corporations Act (BCA); (2) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and annual Certificate of Good Standing; (3) execute a non-resident affidavit confirming no RMI office, employees, real estate, or business activity; (4) no TIN, VAT ID, or tax registration is needed. If the BC later derives RMI-source gross revenue or hires RMI-resident staff, it must register with the TRO and obtain a TIN for Gross Revenue Tax and withholding purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — non-resident domestic corporation under BCA section 116, exempt from RMI income tax, Gross Revenue Tax, franchise tax and succession taxes, subject only to flat annual registry fees. The BC is an entity-level limited-liability corporation, not a pass-through entity. RMI taxation is territorial: income sourced within the RMI can be taxable for resident actors, while foreign e-commerce revenue of a qualifying non-resident BC remains outside the RMI tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The RMI has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime. The sole classification mechanism is the statutory non-resident status election: a BC is non-resident (exempt) if it maintains no place of business and carries on no business in the RMI; Articles may expressly declare this status, and a resident BC may convert by amendment. Commencing business in the RMI automatically revokes the exemption by operation of law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, no GST, and no sales-and-use tax in the Marshall Islands. Indirect-type levies comprise only customs import duties (Customs Act 1990) on goods entering RMI customs territory and Gross Revenue Tax on persons carrying on business in the RMI; neither applies to a non-resident BC selling baby and maternity supplies to foreign customers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0 — not applicable. The US dollar is the sole RMI legal tender. There is no VAT/GST registration threshold and no indirect-tax registration duty for a non-resident BC; Gross Revenue Tax registration arises only upon deriving gross revenue from RMI business activity, which for this exempt entity is zero.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. No real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no e-invoice API mandate exists. Tax substantiation is paper-based; customs entries follow the ASYCUDA electronic clearance procedure for imports into the RMI, while goods dispatched by the non-resident BC directly from outside the RMI require no RMI clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Formally not applicable: the RMI levies no VAT/GST, so there is no zero-rating election or export refund mechanism. Substantively, all export sales by a non-resident BC are automatically outside the RMI indirect tax net; Gross Revenue Tax applies only to RMI-source business revenue, and sales shipped directly to foreign customers are not RMI-source. The 180-day inward remittance benchmark is a banking documentation convention, not a statutory repatriation deadline, as the RMI has no exchange controls.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certificate of Incorporation and annual Certificate of Good Standing from the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
Non-Resident Domestic Corporation status affidavit and board resolution evidencing no RMI business activity
Commercial invoice and packing list for the baby and maternity commodity consignment
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing delivery to a destination outside the RMI
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT receipt evidencing collection of customer proceeds
Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA entry) solely where goods physically transit RMI customs territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The TRO may audit any claimed exemption or non-exposure position. A false non-resident declaration, undisclosed RMI business activity, or falsified export documentation triggers withdrawal of the BCA section 116 exemption, retrospective reassessment of income and Gross Revenue Tax with statutory interest, penalty surcharges (up to 100% of tax for willful evasion), fines and officer imprisonment under the Income Tax Act 1989, and strike-off by the Registrar of Corporations. As no VAT refunds exist, there is no refund-reversal risk; the principal clawback exposure is loss of exempt status and full retrospective taxation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Ministry of Finance) under the Banking Act 1998; no formal central bank exists; the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender and the U.S. Federal Reserve clearing system provides the monetary anchor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands is a fully dollarized jurisdiction. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible and are not subject to exchange controls. A non-resident Business Corporation may remit dividends, service fees, and trading profits to foreign beneficiaries without central-bank approval or convertibility hurdles, provided the company is in good standing and has no outstanding domestic tax obligations (non-resident exempt companies are generally outside Marshall Islands income tax).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements in the Marshall Islands. Export receipts from online sales of maternity and infant care supplies, whether received via SWIFT, card acquirers, or payment platforms, may be retained indefinitely in U.S. dollars, converted into other currencies at the entity's discretion, or used immediately for outbound trade disbursements. No mandatory conversion ratio or time-bound repatriation rule applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Marshall Islands Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for offshore digital EMI providers. The Marshall Islands does not grant standalone EMI licenses, and the Banking Act 1998 requires deposit-taking activity to be conducted by a physically licensed bank. Foreign digital EMI platforms may serve as customer payment gateways, but they cannot act as primary treasury rails for capital escrow or material trade disbursements unless the funds are cleared through a regulated U.S. correspondent bank and settled into a Marshall Islands-licensed account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Standard AML/CFT policy under the Banking Act requires an in-person KYC interview for the ultimate beneficial owner and the designated account signatory, or a notarized verification performed by a recognized attorney or notary public in the presence of a bank representative. The Bank of the Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam generally permit remote opening only where the applicant's resident agent or legal counsel in the Marshall Islands appears physically before the bank and the non-resident directors submit notarized identification documents. Pure remote onboarding without any in-person or locally verified step is typically rejected for a non-resident Business Corporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: a non-resident Business Corporation with bearer shares, nominee shareholders, or an undisclosed principal
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified register of members and ultimate beneficial owners, passport copies of all UBOs, tax identification numbers, a notarized trust deed or nominee declaration, and a current certificate of good standing from the Marshall Islands Registrar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth mismatch in cross-border e-commerce earnings from baby and maternity supplies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements, Stripe and PayPal payout histories, supplier invoices, shipping and customs dossiers, platform traffic or sales reports, and bank statements evidencing the wire trail from platform settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk correspondent usage: inbound transfers routed from offshore digital EMI accounts or cryptocurrency conversion ramps
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of funding by regulated depository institutions in the same legal name, executed purchase or subscription agreements, and a sworn statement confirming the absence of unlicensed money-service-business involvement or cryptocurrency-fiat ramps unless explicitly pre-disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose-code ambiguity for capital injections from the beneficial owner's personal account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed capital subscription resolution, a director's certificate establishing the equity contribution, a bank reference letter for the remitting account, and the applicable payment purpose code (e.g., 'equity capital injection' or 'direct investment equity').

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) screening hits due to name similarity or citizenship exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, UN, EU and local sanctions screening results showing a clear negative match, negative media name-search reports, professional reference letters from a licensed attorney or accountant, and a notarized confirmation of non-sanctions and non-PEP status.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed in U.S. dollars over the correspondent banking system via Fedwire or CHIPS to the receiving Marshall Islands bank. The remitting bank shall issue a SWIFT MT103 containing the beneficiary account number, the exact legal entity name, and a purpose code such as 'K.1 – Equity Injection to Non-Resident Entity' or 'F.1 – Direct Investment Equity'. The receiving bank verifies the UBO against sanctions lists, matches the wire reference to the corporate register, and credits the Capital Escrow Account only after a source-of-funds declaration and capital contribution resolution have been uploaded. Dual-step verification with a telex-free confirmation is required; any inbound payment from a third-party personal account not named in the corporate filing will be pended for enhanced due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement for supplier payments and logistics costs is executed primarily by SWIFT MT103 credit transfers through the Marshall Islands bank's U.S. correspondent, using purpose codes 'T.1 – Payment for Imports of Goods' for purchases of stock-in-trade and 'T.2 – Payment for Services' for freight, customs, and warehousing. For high-value or documentary purchases, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Marshall Islands bank and confirmed by a U.S. or Asian correspondent bank is the preferred rail, affording conditional payment against presentation of bills of lading, commercial invoices, and inspection certificates. Outbound payments to banks in embargoed or high-risk jurisdictions are prohibited absent a specific OFAC license, and real-time name screening is applied to every beneficiary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/GBP deliverable plain-vanilla forwards
USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards for Chinese supplier invoicing
USD/JPY cross-currency swaps supported by documented trade-flow exposure
OTC vanilla FX options limited to hedging of commercial exposures; speculative, leveraged, or crypto-derivative instruments are expressly prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April of each calendar year, reporting on the preceding calendar year; no anniversary-based staggered filing for non-resident business corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after 30 April attracts the statutory penalty assessed by the Registrar; delinquent status suspends good standing, blocks issuance of Certificates of Good Standing, and renders the corporation subject to administrative dissolution (strike-off) after two consecutive missed annual reports, subject to published notice by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident Registered Agent and Registered Office Continuation (agent consent record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, administered through the licensed Marshall Islands resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous statutory condition; agent consent is re-affirmed with the annual cycle and must be effective at the 30 April filing date; any agent resignation requires replacement before the succeeding filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of the resident registered agent authorises the Registrar to appoint a substitute or commence administrative dissolution; failure to maintain a registered office renders filings ineffective and impairs the company's standing in the registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Record Reconfirmation (AML/CFT register held by the registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands resident agent (record accessible to the Financial Intelligence Unit and the Registrar of Corporations on lawful demand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reconfirmed at the annual report cycle (on or before 30 April); any shareholding transfer or new beneficial owner must be recorded within the period set by the Marshall Islands AML/CFT framework (generally 30 days of the change)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or stale beneficial ownership records expose the company and its agent to enforcement under the Marshall Islands AML/CFT legislation, including monetary penalties, agent licence suspension, and potential restrictions on the company's registry status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No asset, revenue, or shareholder-count threshold in the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA) compels a certified audit for a non-resident business corporation. A statutory audit becomes mandatory only where: (i) the company holds a regulated licence (banking, insurance, fiduciary, or trust business); (ii) the articles of incorporation or by-laws require one; or (iii) the Registrar orders an examination of books and records under BCA Section 102 upon a request by shareholders holding the statutory percentage (generally 10% of outstanding voting shares).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The BCA prescribes no statutory GAAP. Financial statements, when prepared for credit, shareholder, or parent-group purposes, conventionally follow US GAAP given the Delaware-derived structure of the BCA; IFRS may be adopted for foreign parent consolidated reporting. No financial statements are filed with or made public by the Registrar for non-resident corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate public UBO declaration is lodged with the Registrar for a standard non-resident business corporation. Beneficial ownership is documented in the AML/CFT register maintained by the licensed resident agent, which re-confirms the ownership structure at each annual cycle (on or before 30 April), updates the record within the prescribed period after any share transfer (generally 30 days), and discloses the record to the Financial Intelligence Unit or Registrar upon lawful demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (and Officers, where appointed)
Minute Book (shareholder and board resolutions and unanimous consents)
Register of Security Interests (charges and mortgages, if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$700–US$1,200 per year (standard independent provider rates for a Marshall Islands resident registered agent, registered office, and compliance administration)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500–US$7,500 per engagement for a voluntary or mandated certified audit of a low-volume e-commerce entity; no audit default applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (no corporate income tax; the RMI levies a 3% Gross Revenue Tax only on revenue from business actually carried on within the Marshall Islands)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident domestic Business Corporations (BCs) that neither conduct business nor derive income from RMI sources are exempt from the 3% Gross Revenue Tax; no payroll tax, capital gains tax, or dividend withholding taxes apply; the only annual fiscal burden is the fixed BCA franchise tax based on authorized capital (typically USD 200 to USD 350)
corporate_income_tax_regime.applicability_note: Loss carryforward provisions are inoperative in practice because no CIT is imposed on a non-resident BC; the 5-year figure is preserved for schema conformity.
